overview: Austria is a landlocked country in Central Europe. Its capital, Vienna, was for centuries the seat of the Habsburg family, who ruled a large empire in central Europe until 1918. Vienna is famous for classical music: Mozart, Haydn and Schubert were Austrian, and Beethoven did much of his work there. Today Austria is a federal republic, a member of the European Union and officially neutral.

geography.text: The Alps cover much of western and southern Austria, where glaciers surround its highest peak, the Grossglockner. The Danube flows across the north of the country from Germany towards Slovakia, passing through Vienna. The east is flatter, with farmland, vineyards and Lake Neusiedl, which Austria shares with Hungary.

history.text: For more than six centuries Austria was ruled by the Habsburg family, whose empire at its height stretched across central Europe. The empire collapsed at the end of the First World War in 1918. Austria was annexed by Nazi Germany in 1938, occupied by the Allies after 1945, and regained full independence in 1955 as a neutral country.

events.title: Siege of Vienna
events.text: An Ottoman army is defeated outside Vienna, helped by the Polish king Jan Sobieski.

events.title: Austria-Hungary
events.text: The empire becomes a dual monarchy shared with Hungary.

events.title: Empire ends
events.text: After defeat in the First World War, Austria becomes a republic.

events.title: Independence restored
events.text: Allied occupation ends and Austria declares permanent neutrality.

government.text: Austria is a federal republic made up of nine states, called Länder, including the capital, Vienna. Voters elect a President every six years and a parliament every five. The Chancellor leads the government. Austria has been neutral since 1955 and is not a member of NATO.

economy.text: Austria is one of the richest countries in the European Union. It has strong manufacturing, including machinery, vehicles and steel, and a huge tourist industry built on Alpine skiing and the culture of Vienna and Salzburg. Much of its electricity comes from hydropower.

culture.text: Austria is famous for classical music. Mozart was born in Salzburg, and Haydn, Schubert and Johann Strauss II were also Austrian. The Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert is watched by millions around the world. Viennese coffee house culture is listed by UNESCO as intangible heritage.

items.title: Mozart
items.text: Born in Salzburg in 1756, he wrote more than 600 works before he died at 35.

items.title: The Sound of Music
items.text: The 1965 film about the von Trapp family was set and filmed around Salzburg.

items.title: Schönbrunn Palace
items.text: The summer home of the Habsburg emperors in Vienna.

sport.text: Alpine skiing is Austria's national sport, and Austrians have won more World Cup ski races than any other nation. Football is also very popular, and Vienna co-hosted Euro 2008 with Switzerland.

items.title: Hahnenkamm
items.text: The downhill race at Kitzbühel, one of the most feared courses in skiing.
Innsbruck has hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

items.title: Euro 2008
items.text: Co-hosted with Switzerland; the final was in Vienna.
